# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- ci-performance-evaluation: Method for finding where a repo's CI time actually goes and what is worth fixing. Use when CI feels slow, when investigating a runtime regression, or when the weekly ci-performance task hands you a finding.
- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.
- extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- generate-project-instructions: Decompose a project into its pack facets (working-style class, technology, aspect, domain) and extract its working instructions into reusable canon packs plus the project's own local packs (.claudinite/local_packs/). Use when a project has no established working style yet, or it exhibits a facet no pack covers — during bootstrap of a fresh/empty repo, or on an uplevel request.
- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- improve-comments: Improve the comments in a repo's own source — delete the ones that restate the code or narrate a past edit, correct the ones that have drifted from what the code now does, and add the why where only a reader's guess carries it. Use when working a repo's comments as their own pass (the tidy-repo pack's improve-comments task), never as a side effect of another change.
- production-retrospective: Design and file the review that comes back on its own once a larger element has lived in production long enough to judge — is it working, misused, overused, underused — read from its real production record against expectations written down when the element was designed. Use when designing a larger element (the brief is authored then), when filing a migration plan's chain (the retrospective is its last link), when a merge completes a design-doc'd element, or when defining a new retrospective class for a pack, a repo, or the fleet.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- single-issue-triage: Triage one open issue and take the first applicable action — close-if-implemented, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, or leave. Use when acting on a single issue; "implemented in main" must be verified against main's current content and the default is to comment, not close (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-issues task hands you issues to triage).
- single-pr-status: Assess one open pull request's landed status — keep-open, or closeable (merged, already-in-main, superseded, stale) — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single PR should stay open, judging by its commits and diff not its title (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-prs task hands you PRs to assess).
- unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.
- verify-in-production: Decide whether a change that has merged can only be proven in production, and if so file the verification that comes back on its own once it is live. Use immediately after the merge, beside the conversation capture — never before, and not on request.
- writing-claudinite-skills: Authoring or changing a skill in the Claudinite corpus — SKILL.md conventions, where a skill's checks and tests live, catalog and pack wiring. Use when creating or editing a pack's skills/<name>/ in the canon; a consumer project's own agent docs are authoring-agent-docs' turf.
- writing-migration-plans: Where a plan and a design live, and how to order a plan's phases so nothing stalls mid-run — the plan is a tracking issue (never a plan document in the repo), the design doc carries only the end state with rationale and alternatives; front-load the out-of-band setup, write ALL the code including the cleanup and take one approval for the stack, then chain every execution step to the verification of the one before it as a queued continuation, and keep the tracking issue append-only while implementing. Use BEFORE writing any DESIGN.md, migration plan, phased implementation plan, rollout or cutover plan — including the moment you are about to create a docs/<initiative>/ file — and when working through a plan's tracking issue.
- writing-tasks: The contract a Claudinite task is written to — the declaration's fields, the code-work and agentic phases, the precondition as the only decision point, ordering, and how a work item converges. - writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.

You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.

Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. {"number":1482,"title":"#1466's rule F fix shipped without a version bump, so no member can receive it","body":"PR #1466 widened janitor rule F (`orphanedParkItems`, `{ knownTaskIds }` → `{ tasks }`) but did **not** bump `packs/claudinite-tasks/pack.mjs`. The version stayed at `60830.5`, which #1464 had already published with the *old* rule.

A member re-vendors a pack directory only when canon's version exceeds the one it has installed. So every member that converged on `60830.5` took #1464's tree — old rule F — stamped it `60830.5`, and can never receive #1466's fix under that version.

## Verified in production

Four members, read straight off `main`:

| repo | `pack.mjs` version | `janitor-rules.mjs` signature |
|---|---|---|
| MissingBulbWebsite | `60830.5` | `orphanedParkItems(open = [], { knownTaskIds ...` |
| VascularColoring | `60830.5` | `orphanedParkItems(open = [], { knownTaskIds ...` |
| EdFringeNow | `60830.5` | `orphanedParkItems(open = [], { knownTaskIds ...` |
| ClaudiniteCanary | `60830.5` | `orphanedParkItems(open = [], { knownTaskIds ...` |

The stamp and the code beside it disagree. Canon at the same version carries `{ tasks }`.

## Observed effect

[{"id":5476860538,"body":"Comment class: other

Investigated as asked, starting from the reproduction: make the same change without a version bump and see whether the checks catch it. **They do. It is not an agent bug and not a bug in the check's logic — it is a gap in what the check is able to ask.** Handing this off with the mechanism established.

## The reproduction says the check works

Branched from `origin/main` (`e846728`), appended a comment line to `packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/janitor-rules.mjs`, bumped nothing, ran `check_the_work.mjs`:

```
[BLOCKING] pack-version-bumped  packs/claudinite-tasks/pack.mjs
  this change edits packs/claudinite-tasks/ but leaves its version at 60831.3
  Fix: raise `version` in packs/claudinite-tasks/pack.mjs to '60831.4' — the version
       is the whole delivery signal, so an edit that does not move it stays in the
       canon forever
```

So the naive form of this failure is caught, blocking, with the right file and the right fix. #1466 did not get through that way.

## What #1466 actually did

The squashed commit `7a73464a` edits five shipping files under `packs/claudinite-tasks/` with `version: '60830.5'` on both sides — apparently the exact thing the check forbids. But it also **adds a `VERSIONS.md` row for 60830.5**, which is not what an agent that simply forgot to bump would produce. That combination is the tell: the branch *did* bump, and the bump was erased by something after CI.

The timeline (UTC), from `packs/claudinite-tasks/pack.mjs`'s own history:

| time | commit | version |
|---|---|---|
| 15:28:54 | `316fc3cb` (#1454) | `60830.4` |
| **20:35:55** | `b7dcf020` (**#1464**) | **`60830.5`** |
| **20:49:36** | `7a73464a` (**#1466**) | **`60830.5`** |
| 21:44:38 | `e4c52479` (#1472) | `60830.6` |

#1466 branched while main was at `60830.4` and bumped to `60830.5` — correctly, and with its `VERSIONS.md` row. **#1464 then merged first, 14 minutes earlier, and took `60830.5` for itself.**

## Both halves reproduced

Reconstructed #1466's branch on the `60830.4` base (`git cherry-pick` of `7a73464a` onto `316fc3cb`, plus the bump to `60830.5` the squash later made invisible) and ran the work checks against that base:

```
$ node engine/checks/check_the_work.mjs --base 316fc3cb
EXIT=0
```

**The PR was legitimately green.** Then merged the colliding commit into it:

```
$ git merge --no-commit --no-ff b7dcf020
Auto-merging packs/claudinite-tasks/pack.mjs      ← no conflict
CONFLICT (content): .../test/queue/janitor-rules.test.mjs   ← a test file; ships to nobody
$ grep -o "version: '[^']*'" packs/claudinite-tasks/pack.mjs
version: '60830.5'
```

`pack.mjs` auto-merges silently, because both sides made the *identical* edit `60830.4` → `60830.5`. Git has nothing to flag. The one conflict is in a test file, which `compute-vendor-set` drops and which therefore cannot warn anybody about a delivery problem.

## Why the check cannot see this

`pack-version-bumped` is `scope: 'work'`, and its own header says why: *"the question is what THIS change did. The tree always contains a version number; only the diff says whether it moved with the content beside it."* Against its own merge-base, #1466 moved the version and recorded the row. Both questions it asks are answered correctly, and yes.

The question nobody asks is a different one, and it is not a work-scope question at all:

> **is the version this change lands on already published on `main` under different content?**

That is a *collision* between two branches, and it is invisible from inside either one. Two PRs racing to bump the same pack both pass, both merge cleanly, and the second one's content ships under a number the fleet already has — so `planPackUpdates` sees `installed >= canon` and never re-fetches. That is #939's failure mode exactly, arriving through a door the check was not built to watch.

**Cost here:** #1466's rule F widening reached no member. The next night's janitor swept with the old `{ knownTaskIds }` code across the whole fleet and closed nothing, which is what this issue was opened on.

## Notes for whoever picks this up

- The 21-hour window `60830.1` → `60831.3` carried **twelve** `claudinite-tasks` versions. At that merge rate the collision window is not an edge case; it is the normal condition, and the same race is available to every pack.
- Recording the row does not protect you — #1466 has a correct `VERSIONS.md` row for `60830.5`, and it is now the *second* row that would claim that number if #1464 had written one too. `versionRecorded` only asks whether a row exists, never whether the version is uniquely claimed.
- Worth checking whether any other pair in that window collided the same way; I only traced `claudinite-tasks`.
- Anything that fixes this has to run where both branches are visible — merge-queue ordering, a world-scope uniqueness assertion over `VERSIONS.md`, or making the bump non-literal so two branches cannot write the same bytes. Choosing between those is the design call, and I have deliberately not made it.

content.content:
DESIGN.md
README.md
check_the_work.mjs
check_the_world.mjs
ci-work-scope.mjs
helpers
report-findings.mjs
run-active-pack-rules.mjs
# Version history

Records for `packs/claudinite-tasks/pack.mjs`'s `version` field, one row per bump.

| Version | Date | What changed |
|---|---|---|
| 60831.5 | 2026-08-31 | Janitor rule E never supersedes an AD-HOC park: every ad-hoc item runs the same task, so a later run of it is evidence about that run and not about this issue's own work. Two verification issues were closed on a third issue's evidence, their own `Verify:` assertion never executed (#1498). |
| 60831.4 | 2026-08-31 | The scheduler run's work-item list reads membership through `isQueueItem`, the shared predicate, rather than the `[claudinite-work]` title prefix — an adopted marked issue keeps the person's own title forever, so the prefix test dropped exactly that class from the one job that releases a blocked item, and ad-hoc items slept days past their `Not-before:` (#1497). The executing-leash reclaim reads such an item's task off its worker path too, so `implement-request`'s `on_interrupt: 'needs-human'` is honoured rather than silently re-queued. |
| 60831.3 | 2026-08-31 | The executor carries every repository VARIABLE as one static `CLAUDINITE_VARS: ${{ toJSON(vars) }}` line, so a task needing a repo variable no longer needs the workflow to name it — the human-merged-PR-per-value coupling that still binds secrets. `vars-bag.mjs` reads it and `taskEnv` unpacks it additively, never overwriting a name the runner's environment already carries; unlike the secrets bag there is no per-task selection, `vars` being non-sensitive by construction. `toJSON(secrets)` stays guarded out of both stubs (#1492). |
| 60831.2 | 2026-08-31 | `converge-item.mjs` is stated and built as what it is: the transition a work-item SESSION performs, planned in code. `instructions.md` step 6 is its only caller, so the REST executor beside it was unreachable — and reached first, making a session meet an error before the path written for it and report that it could not converge. That is what left finished runs to the janitor's 3h leash, which parks them `needs-human-decision`. The file now plans and prints, always on stdout and exit 0; the item is handed in with `--item-file` instead of a second run behind an environment variable. The Actions-side transition is untouched in `executor.mjs` (#1491). |
| 60831.1 | 2026-08-31 | A `task:status:done` terminal closes the issue it stands on, marked or filed — the converge, the executor's code-work close and janitor rule G's merged half alike. `done` is the one outcome with nothing left for anyone to act on; every other terminal still stands on the open issue. Converge's membership test also accepts an item's origin label, so an item adopted before the machine block existed converges in code instead of being refused into a by-hand transition (#1489). |
| 60830.9 | 2026-08-30 | `usage-fold` authorizes `under:.claudinite/local && generated-file-changes` — the tree its aggregate lands in — where `generated-file-changes` alone authorized any GENERATED file in the repo, including another task's delivery (#1479). |
| 60830.8 | 2026-08-30 | `executor.md` and `queue/instructions.md` address their commands from `<here>`, the directory each file sits in, instead of an `<engine>` root that has named nothing since the task surface left `engine/scheduler/`; `instructions.md` never defined the placeholder it used for the terminal transition at all (#1475). |
| 60830.7 | 2026-08-30 | A policy term may name a folder inline, `under:<dir>`, covering any change of any kind inside that directory and nothing outside it — so an ad-hoc request or a task confined to one tree scopes itself without a pack committing a named `merge-rules.json` rule. A list stays a union; `&&` inside a term is the intersection (`under:product-wiki && doc-changes`), every part having to cover the file and every part's whole-diff constraint having to hold. Whitespace around `&&` canonicalizes away, so the stamped trailer stays one token; an unusable path, a composite or a whole-policy word inside an `&&` term invalidates the policy, which authorizes nothing (#1473). |
| 60830.6 | 2026-08-30 | A park can state what would end it. The converge stamps `Ends-when: #<n> closed` on any park given a `--pr`, and janitor rule G closes the item when that target resolves — `done` if it merged, `rejected` if it was closed unmerged. An approval park held an open pull request that nothing ever revisited, which is why rule E excludes the kind; this is what answers it (#1468). |
| 60830.5 | 2026-08-30 | The auto-merge decision becomes a policy: `expected_outcome` collapses to `none`/`pr` (legacy spellings normalize at the door, advisory rename at author time) and a `pr` task declares `automerge` — `nothing`, `anything`, or a list of built-in diff classes `merge-policy.mjs` measures the actual diff against (a pack may extend them as `merge-rules.json` data; anything unresolved fails closed). Landing procedure lives only in `deliver-pr.md` — a task.md describes the changes to perform, never what happens to them. `usage-fold` stops maintaining the `merge=ours` `.gitattributes` line in-run: the pack seeds it at adoption (`seedOps`) and the advisory `generated-merge-driver` drives any repo whose own file predates that. A landing run stamps the `Claudinite-Automerge-Policy:` trailer and the new blocking `automerge-policy-scope` work check re-measures the verdict; the request lane's `Merge:` field now carries any policy expression, `if-narrow` resolving to the `narrow-diff` composite (#1459). |
| 60830.4 | 2026-08-30 | A failed run parks `failure` whatever its worker's triage marker asked for: routing the park by the marker let a worker downgrade its own non-zero exit into a non-blocking lane, so the standing slot freed and the task re-filed daily against an unfixed cause (seven copies in one member, twenty-two in another). The verdict survives as the human-facing instruction in the comment. Janitor rules E and F close a park once a later run of the same task converges clean, or once its task is no longer carried at HEAD — the verdict #1446 gave the executor, applied to the parked set it never picks (#1452). |
| 60830.1 | 2026-08-30 | A task deleted from the checkout while a run is in flight converges its item as obsolete instead of failing it to a human: the executor probes the task directory before it runs anything, and `runCodeWork` names the missing directory rather than letting Node report a missing `/bin/sh` (#1444). |
| 60827.5 | 2026-08-27 | `commentOnly` and its checkable-extension set move to `engine/checks/helpers/code-scanning.mjs`, beside the `stripComments` they were already built on; narrow-diff imports and re-exports them, so the queue's merge verdict and tidy-repo's improve-comments gate answer "comments only" the same way (#1383). |
| 60827.4 | 2026-08-27 | The terminal transition is planned as ops and executed by whichever transport the run has: REST in Actions, and the session's own GitHub tools where a subprocess has no route to them — which is every session `invoke.mjs` fires. The park for a convergence that could not run at all is fixed at the failure park, the only one that holds the task's lane (#1374). |
| 60827.2 | 2026-08-27 | A converge writes only to the item it holds: releasing a dependent a close makes due is the scheduler run's own readiness job alone, never the closing side's. `readyDependents`/`releasedBy` retire from `readiness.mjs` with no caller left (#1373, reversing #892's §15.19). |

content.content:
---
name: merge-to-main
description: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
---

# Merge to main

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent
points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.

1. Load `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request` in one `ToolSearch`.
2. No PR open for the branch? `create_pull_request` (base `main`), body ending `Closes #<issue>`.
3. If the PR has check runs, wait for them to pass. None — merge without waiting.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Don't pre-read
   mergeability; the call fails loudly.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.
6. Capture the conversation:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`
   (in the canon repo: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`). Skip only if
   the repo doesn't declare `claudinite-growth`. A later merge in the same session runs it again.
7. Run the basics pack's
   [verify-in-production](../../../basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md) skill, unasked.
   This step is that skill's **only** trigger — it files against what the squash actually landed,
   which is why it runs here and not when the code was written or the PR opened. It decides
   whether this change needs a production check at all — most don't — and files the issue that
   comes back once the change is live. Never offer the owner to check later instead.

Don't re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge.

# The CANON repo's own CI — Claudinite's test suite + its own conformance sweep
# on every PR. Not consumer wiring (consumers ship no workflow, #385).
name: CI
on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  # Dispatchable so a GITHUB_TOKEN-authored PR (whose push/open GitHub never
  # turns into a pull_request run — the recursion guard) can still get this
  # suite started on its branch: baselining's deliver() and any bot-authored
  # PR flow (#432, #565) dispatch it explicitly.
  workflow_dispatch:
defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash
jobs:
  test-and-conformance:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # Check out the PR's real head, not the synthetic refs/pull/N/merge commit
          # actions/checkout uses by default — otherwise HEAD is an ephemeral merge of
          # the branch into main, which the work-scoped squash-merge-history check would
          # (correctly, for that synthetic commit) flag. This makes CI evaluate exactly
          # what the local Stop hook does: the branch tip. Falls back to github.sha on push.
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
      - name: Unit tests
        # THE test roots — a closed set of FOLDERS, each swept to any depth. Depth is
        # deliberately not enumerated: the previous form spelled out one glob per level of
        # nesting, so a test at an unlisted depth was silently never run — which is exactly
        # how vendoring/'s two files sat outside CI. `**` removes depth from the question;
        # what remains is the root list, and engine-tests/ci-test-roots.test.mjs fails the
        # moment a tracked test lands outside it. Adding a root is a deliberate CI edit;
        # adding a test is not.
        #   engine-tests/            engine/ (migrations included) + the other top-level canon code;
        #                            mirrors engine/'s inner structure, and stays canon-side
        #                            because engine/ ships to consumers exactly as-is (#385)
        #   packs/                   every canon pack's tests, each inside the pack it covers
        #   vendoring/               co-located with the vendor computer/writer they cover,
        #                            the fixture-consumer rehearsal included
        #   dev/tools/               maintainer-side tooling nothing at session time runs
        #   .claudinite/local/packs/ this repo's own local packs — tests live inside the tree
        # nullglob: a root with no tests drops out instead of reaching node as a literal pattern.
        run: |
          shopt -s globstar nullglob
          tests=(engine-tests/**/*.test.mjs packs/**/*.test.mjs vendoring/**/*.test.mjs dev/tools/**/*.test.mjs .claudinite/local/packs/**/*.test.mjs)
          # Deliberately oversubscribed. node --test defaults to one worker per core
          # minus one, which fits a CPU-bound suite; this one spends most of its wall
          # clock waiting — on git plumbing, spawned workers and converge fixtures — so
          # the cores idle at that default (measured on this tree: 106s wall against
          # 187s of user+sys on 4 cores). Doubling the workers: 106s -> 70s, with 16
          # buying only another 2s.
          #
          # TAP goes to a FILE, not the log. 2,448 tests emit ~13,000 lines at 5.3
          # lines each, and a failing run's one `not ok` sits wherever its file
          # finished — while GitHub's job-log API serves only a TAIL and the signed
          # blob URL that would serve the whole thing is proxy-blocked. So a red run
          # said `# fail 1` and nothing more, and five green local re-runs could not
          # name the test (#1170). Printing the failing blocks puts the identity in
          # the tail, where it can actually be read.
          status=0
          node --test --test-concurrency=$(( $(nproc) * 2 )) "${tests[@]}" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/tests.tap" || status=$?
          if [ "$status" -ne 0 ]; then
            echo '::group::failing tests'
            grep -n -A 25 '^not ok' "$RUNNER_TEMP/tests.tap" || echo 'no `not ok` line — the runner died before reporting one'
            echo '::endgroup::'
          fi
          tail -n 12 "$RUNNER_TEMP/tests.tap"
          exit "$status"
      - name: Conformance sweep (world scope)
        # The tree as it stands — the pattern bootstrap wires into consumers.
        run: node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs
      - name: Conformance sweep (work scope)
        # The CHANGE, not the tree: this branch's diff against the base branch, the
        # only scope that can see what a commit did rather than what the repo now
        # holds. It used to run at the session's Stop hook and nowhere else, so a
        # rule about the change was enforced only where a session happened to be.
        #
        # The recipe — fetch the base, skip the engine's own branches, refuse an
        # empty scope, sweep — lives in the engine entry point, which every member
        # vendors and runs by the same one line. This repo is the one that runs it
        # from the repo root instead of the mount.
        #
        # --branch explicitly: the checkout above is a detached head at the PR's real
        # head sha, where `rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` says "HEAD" and no branch name
        # is discoverable — so the skip for engine-authored branches would never fire.
        run: node engine/checks/ci-work-scope.mjs --branch "${{ github.head_ref || github.ref_name }}"
      - name: Growth write-surface gate
        # The lifecycle's capture runs (extract, dedup) are bounded to the repo's own
        # local packs. Unlike promote below, a capture run marks ITSELF — the pinned
        # commit subject its task doc gives it — so the gate self-gates and this step
        # runs on every PR, exiting 0 in ~no time on any other branch.
        run: node .claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/growth-scope-gate.mjs
      - name: Promote write-surface gate
        # The growth promote stage (.claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/tasks/growth-promote/task.md)
        # is the one change bounded to packs/ + skills/ — an ordinary engine PR legitimately edits
        # checks/ and engine/, so this cannot run on every PR. It keys on the promote branch prefix
        # (the task doc pins it) and fails the promote PR if a changed path strays.
        if: contains(github.head_ref, 'growth-promote')
        run: node .claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/promote-scope.mjs

          # (correctly, for that synthetic commit) flag. This makes CI evaluate exactly
          # what the local Stop hook does: the branch tip. Falls back to github.sha on push.
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
      - name: Unit tests
        # THE test roots — a closed set of FOLDERS, each swept to any depth. Depth is
        # deliberately not enumerated: the previous form spelled out one glob per level of
        # nesting, so a test at an unlisted depth was silently never run — which is exactly
        # how vendoring/'s two files sat outside CI. `**` removes depth from the question;
        # what remains is the root list, and engine-tests/ci-test-roots.test.mjs fails the
        # moment a tracked test lands outside it. Adding a root is a deliberate CI edit;
        # adding a test is not.
        #   engine-tests/            engine/ (migrations included) + the other top-level canon code;
        #                            mirrors engine/'s inner structure, and stays canon-side
        #                            because engine/ ships to consumers exactly as-is (#385)
        #   packs/                   every canon pack's tests, each inside the pack it covers
        #   vendoring/               co-located with the vendor computer/writer they cover,
        #                            the fixture-consumer rehearsal included
        #   dev/tools/               maintainer-side tooling nothing at session time runs
        #   .claudinite/local/packs/ this repo's own local packs — tests live inside the tree
        # nullglob: a root with no tests drops out instead of reaching node as a literal pattern.
        run: |
          shopt -s globstar nullglob
          tests=(engine-tests/**/*.test.mjs packs/**/*.test.mjs vendoring/**/*.test.mjs dev/tools/**/*.test.mjs .claudinite/local/packs/**/*.test.mjs)
          # Deliberately oversubscribed. node --test defaults to one worker per core
          # minus one, which fits a CPU-bound suite; this one spends most of its wall
          # clock waiting — on git plumbing, spawned workers and converge fixtures — so
          # the cores idle at that default (measured on this tree: 106s wall against
          # 187s of user+sys on 4 cores). Doubling the workers: 106s -> 70s, with 16
          # buying only another 2s.
          #
          # TAP goes to a FILE, not the log. 2,448 tests emit ~13,000 lines at 5.3
          # lines each, and a failing run's one `not ok` sits wherever its file
          # finished — while GitHub's job-log API serves only a TAIL and the signed
          # blob URL that would serve the whole thing is proxy-blocked. So a red run
          # said `# fail 1` and nothing more, and five green local re-runs could not
          # name the test (#1170). Printing the failing blocks puts the identity in
          # the tail, where it can actually be read.
          status=0
          node --test --test-concurrency=$(( $(nproc) * 2 )) "${tests[@]}" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/tests.tap" || status=$?
          if [ "$status" -ne 0 ]; then
            echo '::group::failing tests'
            grep -n -A 25 '^not ok' "$RUNNER_TEMP/tests.tap" || echo 'no `not ok` line — the runner died before reporting one'
            echo '::endgroup::'
          fi
          tail -n 12 "$RUNNER_TEMP/tests.tap"
          exit "$status"
      - name: Conformance sweep (world scope)
        # The tree as it stands — the pattern bootstrap wires into consumers.
        run: node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs
      - name: Conformance sweep (work scope)
        # The CHANGE, not the tree: this branch's diff against the base branch, the
        # only scope that can see what a commit did rather than what the repo now
        # holds. It used to run at the session's Stop hook and nowhere else, so a
        # rule about the change was enforced only where a session happened to be.
        #
        # The recipe — fetch the base, skip the engine's own branches, refuse an
        # empty scope, sweep — lives in the engine entry point, which every member
        # vendors and runs by the same one line. This repo is the one that runs it
        # from the repo root instead of the mount.
        #
        # --branch explicitly: the checkout above is a detached head at the PR's real
        # head sha, where `rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` says "HEAD" and no branch name
        # is discoverable — so the skip for engine-authored branches would never fire.
        run: node engine/checks/ci-work-scope.mjs --branch "${{ github.head_ref || github.ref_name }}"
      - name: Growth write-surface gate
        # The lifecycle's capture runs (extract, dedup) are bounded to the repo's own
        # local packs. Unlike promote below, a capture run marks ITSELF — the pinned
        # commit subject its task doc gives it — so the gate self-gates and this step
        # runs on every PR, exiting 0 in ~no time on any other branch.
        run: node .claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/growth-scope-gate.mjs
      - name: Promote write-surface gate
        # The growth promote stage (.claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/tasks/growth-promote/task.md)
        # is the one change bounded to packs/ + skills/ — an ordinary engine PR legitimately edits
        # checks/ and engine/, so this cannot run on every PR. It keys on the promote branch prefix
        # (the task doc pins it) and fails the promote PR if a changed path strays.
        if: contains(github.head_ref, 'growth-promote')
        run: node .claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/promote-scope.mjs

one (`nextVersion`); rows 1 to 6 below predate the format and are the plain
counter it replaced.

Comment class: other

Closes #1482

The investigation on the issue established the mechanism and deliberately left the design call. This takes the second of the three options it named — a world-scope uniqueness assertion over `VERSIONS.md` — and lands it with the four collisions already standing in the tree.

## Why this option and not the other two

- **Merge-queue / "require branches up to date"** is a platform setting, which the standing decision keeps for last resort — and at this merge rate (twelve `claudinite-tasks` versions in 21 hours) every PR would have to be updated to `main` and re-run CI serially before it could land.
- **A non-literal bump** replaces the number the whole delivery mechanism is written against.
- **The tree assertion** needs no setting, no new vocabulary, and no new authoring step: `pack-version-bumped` already forces a row for every bump, so *every* collision surfaces as a duplicated row, and the world sweep already runs on every PR **and on every push to `main`** (`ci.yml`). The collision goes red within a minute of the second merge, naming the pack and the number.

It is detection, not prevention, because the collision is between two branches and is invisible from inside either one — which is exactly what the issue's analysis concluded. The remedy the finding prints is the full one: fold the two rows into the one the number carries, and bump to a fresh version to re-deliver the content that was stranded.

## Four collisions were already standing

The issue asked whether any other pair collided the same way. Four, across three packs — each one a change that shipped to nobody under its number:

| pack | version | the two changes |
|---|---|---|
| `claudinite-dashboard` | `60822.2` | `schedule_after:` for `fleet-digest` / the per-park-kind human-work estimate (#1247) |
| `claudinite-dashboard` | `60827.1` | live open-work set (#1389) / `PARKED` as its own display key (#1119) |
| `claudinite-growth` | `60827.1` | `since` on a new check (#1378) / `writing-tasks`' status vocabulary (#1119) |
| `claudinite-tasks` | `60830.5` | auto-merge policy (#1459) / the pack-rename item fix (#1461) — the issue's own case |

Each pair is folded into the one row its number carries, with a clause saying the number was claimed twice. No re-delivery bump is needed: all three packs have since bumped past (`60827.2`, `60830.8`, `60831.5`), so every member converging since holds both halves.

## See it fail

Run against the real tree before the repair: 4 blocking findings, exactly those four pairs, and nothing else in the corpus. After the repair, `check_the_world` is 0 blocking and the whole suite (2,844 tests) is green.

## Folders touched

```
.claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/worldRules/  new pack-version-claimed-once rule — no two rows of a
                                                    pack's VERSIONS.md claim the same version
.claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/workRules/   pack-version-bumped exports rowVersions (the row shape
                                                    defined once); versionRecorded now reads it
packs/claudinite-dashboard/, claudinite-growth/,    the four duplicate VERSIONS.md rows folded into one row
packs/claudinite-tasks/                             per version
```

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

input.title: One pack version, one tree — ask the delivery question again on main
input.body:
Comment class: correction

Closes #1482

The first push of this branch measured the wrong thing, and the owner's question is what corrected it. **The defect is that a pack's content landed under a version already published to the fleet.** A duplicated `VERSIONS.md` row is evidence of that having happened, not the defect itself — and a check that only reads the log can only see collisions where both sides happened to record a row.

## The gate that was missing

`pack-version-bumped` asks what THIS change did, against the base the branch forked from. On #1466's branch the version *had* moved (`60830.4` → `60830.5`) and the row *was* recorded, so green was the truth. #1464 then merged first and took `60830.5`, and `pack.mjs` auto-merged because both sides wrote identical bytes. Nothing was left to see from inside either branch.

But it is plainly visible on `main`. Commit `7a73464a`, the one this issue was opened on:

```
$ git checkout 7a73464a
$ node .claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/pack-delivery-on-main.mjs
pack-delivery-on-main: FAIL — 1 pack(s) landed content that no member will be sent (vs HEAD^):
  - packs/claudinite-tasks/pack.mjs: this change edits packs/claudinite-tasks/ but
    leaves its version at 60830.5
```

Four shipping files changed; the version sits exactly where its parent left it. So the same rule is asked again with a different base — a branch against where it forked, a push to `main` against what `main` actually held (the push event's `before`, so a push carrying several commits is judged as one delivery; the parent otherwise). It runs in `ci.yml` on push to `main` only, and only this rule: the branch-shaped rules (a task, an issue, a session behind the change) have no answer on a squashed merge commit, while delivery still does.

Not the whole work sweep, not a platform setting, not a change to how a version is written — one rule, asked once more, at the only point where both branches exist.

## The log check stays, as the record's own guard

`pack-version-claimed-once` (world scope: no two rows of a pack's `VERSIONS.md` claim the same version) is what surfaced the collisions that already happened — the new gate can only see pushes made after it exists. Four were standing, across three packs:

| pack | version | the two changes |
|---|---|---|
| `claudinite-dashboard` | `60822.2` | `schedule_after:` for `fleet-digest` / the per-park-kind human-work estimate (#1247) |
| `claudinite-dashboard` | `60827.1` | live open-work set (#1389) / `PARKED` as its own display key (#1119) |
| `claudinite-growth` | `60827.1` | `since` on a new check (#1378) / `writing-tasks`' status vocabulary (#1119) |
| `claudinite-tasks` | `60830.5` | auto-merge policy (#1459) / the pack-rename item fix (#1461) — this issue's own case |

Each pair is folded into the one row its number carries. No re-delivery bump is needed: all three packs have since bumped past (`60827.2`, `60830.8`, `60831.5`), so every member converging since holds both halves.

## See it fail

- The gate, against `7a73464a` in a real checkout: exit 1, naming the pack and the version (above).
- The log rule, against the real tree before the repair: 4 blocking findings, exactly those four pairs, nothing else in the corpus.
- After: `check_the_world` 0 blocking, work scope clean, whole suite 2,849 tests green.

## Folders touched

```
.claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/            pack-delivery-on-main.mjs — the push-to-main delivery
                                                   gate, reusing the pack-version-bumped rule over two
                                                   commits instead of a working tree
.claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/worldRules/  pack-version-claimed-once — no two rows of a pack's
                                                   VERSIONS.md claim the same version
.claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/workRules/   pack-version-bumped exports rowVersions (the row shape
                                                   defined once); versionRecorded reads it
.github/workflows/                                 ci.yml runs the gate on push to main, passing
                                                   github.event.before as the base
packs/claudinite-dashboard/, claudinite-growth/,   the four duplicate VERSIONS.md rows folded into one
packs/claudinite-tasks/                            row per version
```

---

content.text: {"id":"4402090834","url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1523"}

**Comment class: correction.** You're right, and my first pass measured the symptom.

The problem is the second one: **code changed and the version didn't move** — content landed under a number the fleet already had, so `planPackUpdates` saw `installed >= canon` and never re-fetched. The duplicated `VERSIONS.md` rows are only evidence that this happened; a log-reading check can also only catch the cases where both sides happened to record a row.

What I'd missed is that the defect is directly visible on `main`. Commit `7a73464a` (#1466's squash) changed four shipping files under `packs/claudinite-tasks/` while `pack.mjs` sat at its parent's `60830.5`. `pack-version-bumped` already asks exactly that question — it was just never asked with `main`'s own base, because on a push to `main` the work scope sees `HEAD == origin/main` and skips.

So I added the gate: the same rule, run against what `main` held before the push (`github.event.before`, else the parent), in `ci.yml` on push to `main`. Against a real checkout of `7a73464a` it fails and names the file and the version. Only that rule runs there — the branch-shaped rules have no answer on a squashed merge commit, delivery still does.

I kept the `VERSIONS.md` uniqueness rule, but demoted to what it actually is: the guard on the record, and the thing that surfaced the four collisions that already happened (the gate can only see pushes made after it exists).

```
.claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/            pack-delivery-on-main.mjs — the push-to-main gate,
                                                   reusing pack-version-bumped over two commits
.claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/worldRules/ pack-version-claimed-once — no two rows of a pack's
                                                   VERSIONS.md claim the same version
.claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/workRules/  pack-version-bumped exports rowVersions;
                                                   versionRecorded reads it
.github/workflows/                                 ci.yml runs the gate on push to main
```

- [`pack-delivery-on-main.mjs`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/issue-1482-dmv0zo/.claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/pack-delivery-on-main.mjs) · [its test](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/issue-1482-dmv0zo/.claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/test/pack-delivery-on-main.test.mjs) · [`ci.yml`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/issue-1482-dmv0zo/.github/workflows/ci.yml)

input.body:
Comment class: correction

Closes #1482

**What fixes the problem:** CI now runs `pack-version-bumped` a second time — on every push to `main`, against what `main` held before that push. That is the only point at which the two racing branches both exist, and the version-not-moved failure is plainly visible there.

## Why the existing check could not catch it

`pack-version-bumped` asks what THIS change did, against the base its branch forked from. #1466 forked when `main` was at `60830.4`, bumped to `60830.5`, recorded its row — correct, and green. #1464 merged 14 minutes earlier and took `60830.5` for itself. `pack.mjs` then auto-merged with no conflict, because both sides had written the identical bytes `60830.4` → `60830.5`.

The result on `main` is the defect in plain sight: a commit that edits four shipping files under `packs/claudinite-tasks/` while `pack.mjs` sits at its parent's version. Members that had already converged keep #1464's tree stamped `60830.5` forever, because `planPackUpdates` reads `installed >= canon` and never re-fetches.

## The gate

`.claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/pack-delivery-on-main.mjs` runs the same rule over two commits instead of a working tree. Against a real checkout of the commit this issue was opened on:

```
$ git checkout 7a73464a
$ node .claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/pack-delivery-on-main.mjs
pack-delivery-on-main: FAIL — 1 pack(s) landed content that no member will be sent (vs HEAD^):
  - packs/claudinite-tasks/pack.mjs: this change edits packs/claudinite-tasks/ but
    leaves its version at 60830.5
    raise `version` in packs/claudinite-tasks/pack.mjs to '60831.1' — the version is
    the whole delivery signal, so an edit that does not move it stays in the canon forever
```

Details that matter:

- **The base is the push, not the last commit.** `github.event.before` where CI supplies one, so a push carrying several commits is judged as one delivery; the parent otherwise; nothing to judge when neither resolves.
- **Only this rule runs there.** A member's maintenance merges and this repo's own automation land on `main` too, and the branch-shaped rules (a task, an issue, a session behind the change) have no answer on a squashed merge commit. Delivery still does.
- **Not a platform setting.** Merge-queue ordering or "require branches up to date" would also close this, but at twelve `claudinite-tasks` versions in 21 hours every PR would have to be updated to `main` and re-run CI serially before it could land.

It is detection at the moment of landing, not prevention — the collision does not exist until the second merge. The remedy it prints is a fresh version for the pack, which re-delivers the content that landed here.

## Not in this PR

The four collisions already standing in the corpus (`claudinite-dashboard` twice, `claudinite-growth`, `claudinite-tasks`) leave duplicate `VERSIONS.md` rows behind. A check for those, and the repair of the four, goes in its own PR at the owner's request.

## Folders touched

```
.claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/   pack-delivery-on-main.mjs — the push-to-main delivery gate,
                                          running the pack-version-bumped rule over two commits
.github/workflows/                        ci.yml runs it on push to main, passing github.event.before
```

`pack-version-claimed-once` (world scope): no two rows of a pack's `VERSIONS.md` claim the same version. Two rows for one number means "what did version N change?" has two answers, and one of the two changes reached no member under it.

It is not a second delivery gate. `pack-delivery-on-main.mjs` catches a collision as it lands; a collision that landed *before* that gate existed left no red run behind, only the rows — which is what this asks the tree about, on every PR and every push to `main`.

| `claudinite-dashboard` | `60827.1` | live open-work set (#1389) / `PARKED` as its own display key (#1119) |
| `claudinite-growth` | `60827.1` | `since` on a new check (#1378) / `writing-tasks`' status vocabulary (#1119) |
| `claudinite-tasks` | `60830.5` | auto-merge policy (#1459) / the pack-rename item fix (#1461) — #1482's own case |

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).

- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

# The CANON repo's own CI — Claudinite's test suite + its own conformance sweep
# on every PR. Not consumer wiring (consumers ship no workflow, #385).
name: CI
on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  # Dispatchable so a GITHUB_TOKEN-authored PR (whose push/open GitHub never
  # turns into a pull_request run — the recursion guard) can still get this
  # suite started on its branch: baselining's deliver() and any bot-authored
  # PR flow (#432, #565) dispatch it explicitly.
  workflow_dispatch:
defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash
jobs:
  test-and-conformance:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

        # how vendoring/'s two files sat outside CI. `**` removes depth from the question;

        # adding a test is not.

        #                            because engine/ ships to consumers exactly as-is (#385)

        #   vendoring/               co-located with the vendor computer/writer they cover,
        #                            the fixture-consumer rehearsal included
        #   dev/tools/               maintainer-side tooling nothing at session time runs

        # (the task doc pins it) and fails the promote PR if a changed path strays.

input.title: Judge a push onto the base branch instead of skipping it
input.body:
Closes #1482

## What fixes the problem

`check_the_work` was never wrong. `pack-version-bumped` is a work-scope rule and it works — run it over #1466's landed commit today and it fails, naming the file and the version:

```
$ node engine/checks/check_the_work.mjs --changed --base HEAD^   # at 7a73464a
[BLOCKING] pack-version-bumped  packs/claudinite-tasks/pack.mjs
  this change edits packs/claudinite-tasks/ but leaves its version at 60830.5
```

It was never *asked*. On #1466's branch the version had moved from where the branch forked, honestly, and the same was true of #1464's branch. The collision exists only once both are on `main` — and `ci.yml` already runs on push to `main`, already runs this exact sweep there. The entry point declined:

```
work scope: skipped — HEAD is origin/main, so there is no change to judge
```

So this is one behaviour change in `engine/checks/ci-work-scope.mjs`. When HEAD is the base branch tip, that is a push, and the change to judge is the push: base becomes what the branch held before it, read from `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH` — the payload Actions writes unasked, so no workflow gains an input and this converges with the engine to every member. A developer's clone sitting on `main` has no such payload and still skips.

Driven end to end through the real entry point against `7a73464a`, with `origin/main` pinned there and the real event payload:

```
work scope: 8 changed file(s) vs b7dcf02
[BLOCKING] pack-version-bumped  packs/claudinite-tasks/pack.mjs
  Fix: raise `version` in packs/claudinite-tasks/pack.mjs to '60831.1'
```

The same run against today's `main` tip is clean, so a landed merge does not start failing on rules written for a branch.

## Not in this PR

The four `VERSIONS.md` rows this collision left duplicated, and the world-scope rule that found them, are #1527 / #1529.

You're right on both counts, and the second follows from the first.

**Did `check_the_work` work?** Yes, entirely. `pack-version-bumped` catches #1466 today, unmodified — I ran the real runner over `7a73464a` with base `HEAD^` and it fails, naming `packs/claudinite-tasks/pack.mjs` and the `60830.5` left behind. Nothing was missing from the rule, the runner, or the pack.

**So why a new workflow?** There was no reason. `ci.yml` already triggers on `push: branches: [main]` and already runs the work sweep there. It just declined — `work scope: skipped — HEAD is origin/main, so there is no change to judge`. I built a parallel module and a fifth CI step to re-ask a question the existing step was already standing in the right place to ask.

[#1523](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1523) is now one behaviour change in [`engine/checks/ci-work-scope.mjs`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/issue-1482-dmv0zo/engine/checks/ci-work-scope.mjs): when HEAD is the base branch tip, that is a push, and the push is the change to judge — base becomes what the branch held before it, from `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH`, the payload Actions writes unasked. ## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

message.content: Explain the change in 1523 in the simplest terms. What was the issue, what was the fix?

content.text:
Claudinite loaded, 9 packs, 38 checks, 14,500 rule tokens, 23 available skills, 550 personal preference tokens.

**The problem**

A pack only reaches members when its version number goes up. Two branches can each bump `claudinite-tasks` to `60830.5`. Each is honest against its own starting point — neither branch can see the other. Whichever lands second ships its content under a version members already have, so nobody ever receives it. That's what happened to [#1466](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1466).

**Why the existing check didn't catch it**

`pack-version-bumped` catches it fine. But it runs on "the change" — and the only place both branches exist at once is `main`, after the merge. CI already runs the sweep on push to `main`; the entry point just declined there, printing *"HEAD is origin/main, so there is no change to judge"* — because on your laptop, sitting on `main` genuinely means no change.

**The fix**

In CI, sitting on `main` isn't idle — it's a merge that just landed. So [`ci-work-scope.mjs`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/issue-1482-dmv0zo/engine/checks/ci-work-scope.mjs) now asks: *was this a push?* If yes, judge the push — base becomes where `main` stood before it, read from the event payload Actions already writes. Same rules, same runner, one more moment they get asked.

Off CI there's no payload, so a clone on `main` still skips exactly as before.

```
engine/checks/   ci-work-scope.mjs — "HEAD is the base branch" stops being a skip
                 and becomes a work scope against the push's own base
```

> ⚠️ Still open: [#1523](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1523) and [#1529](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1529) await review.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.
